blocks.x: Warehouse twin for dynamic slotting, pick rate up 17% and peak-season temp labor down 23%

A third-party logistics provider: Logistics operations lose money in the gaps: idle fleets, dwell time and manual re-planning. The Achala program started with the route economics —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.

The baseline quarter walked the floor: pick rates 14% below benchmark, fast movers parked in corners the original layout chose years ago, and every peak season bought temp labor to compensate for geometry.
Slotting wisdom existed as folklore, two veterans could improve any layout by eye, but the eye doesn't scale to 34,000 SKUs and it doesn't stay when they retire.

We built the warehouse twin: order history, velocity and affinity resolved into a live flow model, re-slotting recommendations simulated against the twin before anyone touches a shelf, move batches sequenced to protect the operating day, and the veterans' heuristics encoded as constraints the model respects. The floor improves continuously now, and quietly.
